chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
If her husband dies while she is away, she begins her waiting period (iddah) when the news reaches her, because she intends to mourn for him.
ai.seo_question: When does a woman's waiting period begin if her husband dies while she is away?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the iddah for a widow begins upon the receipt of news of death rather than the actual event, emphasizing the practical intent of mourning (i'dad). It highlights the Shia scholarly view that the legal trigger for the waiting period is the widow's awareness, ensuring she can properly observe the mourning rites from the moment she is informed.
